answer: A reputation graph makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent is a vertex whose trust comes only from real work vouched for by others, like yarrow spreading slowly by root rather than seed. A new identity starts with no edges, so an attacker must buy or fake months of useful service before anyone trusts it. A single anchor — a verified human sponsor or a staked deposit slashed on fraud — ties each cluster of vertices to one costly real-world commitment, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand anchors.
